Merge Sort Explained

Merge sort splits an array in half, sorts each half recursively and then merges the two sorted halves into one sorted array. It runs in O(n log n) time in every case and needs linear extra space for the merge step.

The merge step walks both halves with two indices and always copies the smaller front element, which makes the sort stable. Because the recursion depth is logarithmic, the algorithm behaves predictably even on adversarial inputs.

In practice, hybrid versions switch to insertion sort for tiny sub-arrays to cut the constant factor, and external variants apply the same idea to data on disk.
